text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Yugoslav president Zoran Lilic promises state support for Bor copper complex and entire economy of the region.
- Pre-election silence begins in Yugoslavia ahead of November 3 elections. According to the law, final results within 72 hours.
- Yugoslav and Macedonian chambers of commerce sign cooperation agreement. Joint firms and production programmes to benefit economies of both countries.
- Association of Yugoslav banks proposes to the National Bank of Yugoslavia that it reduce discount rate, currently 4.5 percent per month.
- Payment of first part of September pensions in Serbia next week.
- Serbian power company postpones final decision on electricity consumption quota.
- Head of the Belgrade public transport drivers' trade union Dragoljub Stosic to be detained in prison for 30 days for instigating "illegal" protests.
- Yugoslavia and Russia sign four agreements on economic cooperation -- on liberalisation of trade and on cooperation in agriculture, plant quarantine and veterinary sciences.
- High representative for Bosnia Carl Bildt puts the "brakes" on Bosnia reconstruction programme. No economic assistance as long as campaign of destruction continues.
- Bosnian Serbs meet delegation of the European Bank. Privatisation a condition for investments.

- After Yugoslav foreign minister Milan Milutinovic's visit to Zagreb, real normalisation of relations still far away. Many open questions -- number of missing persons and prisoners on both sides, status of Prevlaka peninsula, legal succession, regular road and rail transport, abolition of visas, return of refugees.

- "My calculations are different from those of economists," says National Bank of Yugoslavia vice governor Ratko Banovic, insisting there are no grounds for devaluation and that dinar and monetary situation will remain stable.
- A year of peace. Anniversary of Dayton peace talks.
- IMR and Dinara sign deal with Hungarian Raba worth 45 million German marks for the production of diesel engines and exchange of parts and components.
- Doboj police detain Ferid Halilovic, former security chief at prison camp for Serbs in Odzak and member of Croat unit, on charges of war crimes. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
